svg.text: Hover a frame for details. Click to zoom, double-click the background to reset, Ctrl+F to search.
select d.dept_name AS dept_name,round(AVG(s.salary),2) AS avg_salary
where ((s.emp_no = de.emp_no) and (d.dept_no = de.dept_no) and (de.to_date = DATE'9999-01-01') and (s.to_date = DATE'9999-01-01'))
Width = time for that operation (wider = slower). Bottom = query root; top = leaf table access.
Click a frame to zoom in on that operation. Ctrl+F to search. Hover for time, rows and loops.
Warnings below refer to specific operations by label (e.g. TABLE SCAN [users]).
Row estimate off by 10× or more: salaries (estimated 1, actual 11 rows per loop, 11× under)
1 sort operation(s) — 9 rows; may use disk-based filesort

• Refresh statistics with ANALYZE TABLE salaries. If a filter on a non-indexed column stays misestimated, add a histogram: on MySQL 8.0+, ANALYZE TABLE salaries UPDATE HISTOGRAM ON <column> WITH 100 BUCKETS; on MariaDB, ANALYZE TABLE salaries PERSISTENT FOR COLUMNS (<column>)

INDEXES (). Why: the optimizer picks join order and access methods from these estimates. InnoDB recalculates persistent statistics on its own only after about 10% of a table's rows change, and on MariaDB, under the default use_stat_tables=PREFERABLY_FOR_QUERIES, ANALYZE TABLE
collects column statistics and histograms only when you add PERSISTENT FOR.
• Add indexes on filter/join columns to avoid full table scans
• Increase sort_buffer_size or add an ordered index to avoid filesort
